findings.claim: The global CleanUpService ticker in cleanup.go was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. As a result, all cleanup jobs (snapshots, query history, short URLs, temp users, annotations, etc.) run 10x as often, and the loop can run nearly continuously when a run takes longer than a minute.
The per-run timeout at cleanup.go:89 is still 9 minutes, a value sized for the old 10-minute cadence. With the 1-minute ticker, cleanup runs can overlap or go back-to-back.

The annotation cleanup closures in xorm_store.go contain six r.log.Error calls (lines 534/537/554/557/576/579) that log routine operational information. These calls fire at Error level on every batch, including successful and empty ones.
The cleanup log statements include the full ids slice, which can contain thousands of annotation IDs and produce very large log lines.
The cleanup log statements log 'err' after the error has already been checked and returned, so the logged value is always nil.

deleteByIDs in xorm_store.go (around lines 605-608) chooses between paths by checking r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit instead of len(ids) > sqliteParameterLimit. Because of this, small final batches still use the inlined-ID path when the configured batch size is large.
The SQLite inlined-ID path in deleteByIDs builds the IN list by string concatenation (fmt.Sprintf) in a loop, which takes quadratic time in the batch size.

The non-SQLite path in deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID with no cap. MySQL and Postgres reject statements with more than 65535 bind parameters, so a batch size above 65535 makes every DELETE fail.
The deleteByIDs comment says SQLite's parameter limit is 999. That limit applies only before SQLite 3.32 (32766 after), and the test name references the 3.32 limit.

deleteByIDs has two SQL paths: inlined IDs for SQLite above 999, and placeholders elsewhere. The IDs are int64 values read from the DB, so a single path would be sufficient, and the second path adds a GetDBType branch, sqliteParameterLimit, args/asAny, and a migrator import.

The fetch->log->delete->log closure is copied three times (by time, by count, tags) with opaque x, y temporaries in xorm_store.go (528-539, 548-559, 570-581). The copies already differ in their log wording.

The test case 'running the max count delete again should not remove any annotations' now seeds fresh data for each case, so it no longer runs cleanup a second time over prior state. Idempotency of a repeated run is not tested, and the test name does not match what it does.

In TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp, t.Cleanup is registered only after data seeding and assertions (cleanup_test.go:116 seeds, :120 registers). A failure before registration leaves rows in the shared DB that affect later subtests.
Test seeding sets explicit IDs (ID: int64(i+1)). On Postgres this does not advance annotation_id_seq, so later inserts that use the sequence can hit duplicate keys.

createTestAnnotations in cleanup_test.go (273-291) duplicates the 500-row InsertMulti chunk loop for annotations and annotation tags. It also calls require.NoError inside the DB callback and then returns nil.

coverage: pooled issues; severity and verdict are placeholders
